_about: Vocabulary of the server-side document binding (src/document_binding.py): how documents name a manufacturer, a model family, a body style, a propulsion, a drivetrain. Families are matched as whole words, spaces/hyphens optional; a longer family that extends a shorter one (corolla cross vs corolla) is masked out before the shorter one is searched, and a fact whose context names the longer family is NOT about the shorter one. Body/propulsion/drivetrain keys are the Level 1.5 normalized values. Editing this file changes binding with no code change; nothing in Python names a brand or model. propulsion_weak_terms count as a propulsion match only for a target of that propulsion and only when no conflicting propulsion is named (a plain 'electric' is also said of hybrids).

catalog_trim_aliases._about: Non-prefix written forms of government catalog trim tokens (src/variant_map.catalog_trim_matches): a catalog token matches the document words listed here, in order, besides the prefix rule (CORE PERF ~ 'Core Performance', STAND RANGE ~ 'Standard Range') and the token join (BLACKEDITION ~ 'Black Edition'). Generic abbreviations only, never a brand name.

model_code_table._about: The regulatory safety-equipment table Israeli importer pages must publish: a code column and a model description column. Its code is the government degem_cd (verified against the Level 1.5 catalog for PR #42); src/variant_map reads such a table as gov_model_code identities.

variant_designations._about: PR #43: regular expressions (over normalized, lower-case text) of engine / powertrain VERSION designations a document uses to tell versions of one model apart ('55 TFSI e', '40TFSI', 'TFSIe', '4xe', 'P400'). A designation is written into a region's identity (src/variant_map.identity_vector, key `designation`, compact form '55tfsie'); two regions with different designations are never the same variant; a hybrid / plug-in document that names two or more designations (or states two or more distinct powers) never identifies the variant by displacement alone (document_binding.bind, H1). Generic patterns only, never a model name. PR #45: the reversed order of Israeli used-car titles ('TFSI 45') is the same designation (compact form '45tfsi').

relative_variant_terms._about: PR #43 (H2): comparative references to ANOTHER version of the model. A value whose own clause uses one ('the more senior one adds 22" wheels') is about that other version: heading-level evidence (a section heading, the document's trim) never binds it to a trim or technical variant; it binds at most body_powertrain (binding flag relative_variant_reference).

gearbox_terms._about: PR #43 (H4): a gearbox named as part of a version name ('1.5 TSI DSG', '40 TFSI S tronic') is part of the region identity (key `gearbox`); a region whose gearbox contradicts the target's government transmission (Level 1.5 `automatic`) stays unresolved.

body_subvariants._about: PR #45 (R3): body SUB-VARIANT words that tell two models of one catalog family apart (Q3 / Q3 Sportback, A4 / A4 Avant, 4 Series / 4 Series Gran Coupe): the government catalog key does not separate them, so binding reads them from names. A sub-variant named in a document's identity zone (title / H1 / URL words of a segment naming the target family) that the target's commercial name / government model name does not contain is a body mismatch (veto at the body cap); on an Israeli single-version page the reverse holds too (a target whose name contains the sub-variant needs it in the page's title / H1 / URL). `implies_body`: the Level 1.5 body_normalized the word implies; a word whose implied body IS the target's body is never a mismatch (a Corolla wagon on a 'Touring Sports' page). Terms of a longer key mask shorter ones ('gran coupe' before 'coupe').

body_market_names._about: PR #47 (A1): the Israeli market names of a model's body sub-model, keyed by Latin manufacturer slug | model family (identity vocabulary `manufacturers` / `model_families` keys) and Level 1.5 body_normalized, plus generic names per body. The IL version-page resolver (src/il_version_pages.py) puts the target body's first Hebrew / Latin name in its site searches ({body_he} / {body_en}) and ranks a candidate +2 when its URL / title names the target body, -3 when it names another body sub-model of the family (family names of the other bodies, generic names of the other bodies). Unknown family or body: nothing (no query word, no rank change). Data only: nothing in Python names a brand or a model.

trim_word_forms_he._about: PR #47 (A3): Hebrew written forms of generic trim words, used to read a Hebrew version name (carzone's compare columns: "ביזנס אדישן") as Latin trim words before the catalog-trim rules (src/variant_map.catalog_trim_matches) compare it with the government trim (BUSINESS EDI). Generic trim vocabulary only, never a brand or model name; a Hebrew word missing here never matches (fail-closed).

approval_routes._about: The government approval type (sug_tkina_cd / sug_tkina_nm) -> the open-data identity route (src/gov_registry.approval_route, src/open_data/match.py). Anything else is `unknown` (the stricter gate of both routes).

open_data_make_aliases._about: Reviewed EXTRA make spellings per tozar that normalization (data/make_canonical.json) does not produce: added to the generated aliases, never a replacement. The canonical makes and their normalized spellings come from data/make_canonical.json; a model-gated make (MINI, CUPRA, RAM, VAUXHALL) is never listed here (it would count by make alone).

open_data_model_aliases._about: Optional per `tozar|family` model spellings of the open datasets when the family word alone does not match (a whole word / phrase of the dataset's model text).
